summary: No PII leakage, error-isolation intact, mass-assignment defended. The telegram_callback_query event metadata carries only projectId, chatId, and the internal callback_data code marker ({executionId}:{buttonIndex}) — never from.first_name/last_name/username. advanceOnCallback is best-effort swallow-all (Task 5) and stays inside the worker's try/catch(Throwable); no extra local swallow was added that could hide a genuine worker failure path. CallbackQuery DTO uses @JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown=true) (mass-assignment defense). Idempotency/re-entry guard (DONE -> no-op before any side effect) is preserved for callback updates.

findings.finding: from is intentionally not surfaced into metadata; callbackQuery_eventCarriesNoPii asserts no first/last name or username value leaks. data marker is an internal code, not PII.
advanceOnCallback (swallow-all) is not wrapped in a redundant local try/catch, so real worker faults still reach handleFailure (FAILED + scrub + rethrow). A bad callback cannot break the webhook ack.
Owner authorization and CAS-scoping live in advanceOnCallback (Task 5) by design; the worker correctly forwards projectId+chatId+data and does not re-implement authz.
